chains.roles: source: a 2D density/saliency/embedding raster (UMAP kernel-density, attention map, loss landscape) exported as GeoTIFF -> transform: TauDEM treats scalar intensity as elevation and runs pit-fill + D-infinity flow accumulation + stream/watershed extraction -> sink: SedonaDB ingests the basin polygons (GeoParquet) for SQL queries over cluster catchments
chains.glue: hop1: raster written as single-band GeoTIFF with a fabricated affine geotransform (magick convert map.png -depth 32 gray:- then wrap with a .tfw/gdal_translate; TauDEM only needs a valid GeoTIFF, not real georeferencing). hop2: TauDEM file chain of GeoTIFFs (fel/ang/sca/src) + net.shp vector. hop3: net.shp / watershed w.tif -> polygonized GeoParquet read by SedonaDB via ST_Read/GeoParquet
chains.emergent_capability: Unsupervised, parameter-light hierarchical cluster segmentation of any 2D field by literally computing its ridgelines and drainage basins.
chains.sketch: magick saliency.png -colorspace Gray -depth 32 gray.tif; gdal_translate -a_srs EPSG:3857 -a_ullr 0 1000 1000 0 gray.tif dem.tif; mpiexec -n 4 pitremove -z dem.tif -fel fel.tif; mpiexec -n 4 dinfflowdir -fel fel.tif -ang ang.tif -slp slp.tif; mpiexec -n 4 areadinf -ang ang.tif -sca sca.tif; mpiexec -n 4 threshold -ssa sca.tif -src src.tif -thresh 200; mpiexec -n 4 streamnet -fel fel.tif -p p.tif -ad8 sca.tif -src src.tif -ord ord.tif -tree tree.dat -coord coord.dat -net net.shp -w w.tif  # then SELECT * FROM sedona.read_geoparquet('basins.parquet') in SedonaDB
chains.pattern: wrong-domain-as-substrate (treat a non-terrain scalar field as a DEM)
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real: watershed/flow-accumulation gives a physically-grounded hierarchical partition (basins nest, ridgelines are exact separatrices) that neither k-means nor a saliency tool produces; who it's for = ML/vis researchers wanting deterministic, tuning-free cluster boundaries; not novelty-from-friction because the hydrology and the density-topology genuinely share the ridge/basin abstraction.
chains.fragile_seam: The fabricated geotransform must keep pixel spacing sane or D-infinity slope angles distort; noisy rasters over-segment, so a pre-smoothing/pit-depth threshold is doing real work.

chains.roles: source: smof filters/tidies a FASTA file to a clean set of sequences -> transform: awk tokenizes each sequence into a space-separated codon (or fixed-k) 'sentence', then colibri-core builds a compressed pattern model and extracts skipgrams/flexgrams -> sink: a ranked list of spaced sequence motifs (fixed anchors with variable gaps)
chains.glue: hop1: smof stdout FASTA -> hop2: awk emits one whitespace-tokenized line per record (a 'corpus'); colibri-classencode corpus.txt -> corpus.colibri.cls + .colibri.dat -> hop3: colibri-patternmodeller consumes the binary .dat/.cls and prints skipgrams
chains.emergent_capability: A Finnish-morphology-grade skipgram engine becomes a de novo spaced-motif finder for DNA/protein, because a flexgram (fixed tokens + variable-width gap) is exactly a biological spaced motif.
chains.sketch: smof filter -l 60 seqs.fa | smof clean | awk '/^>/{if(s)print s; s=""; next}{gsub(/.{3}/,"& "); s=s $0}END{print s}' > corpus.txt; colibri-classencode corpus.txt; colibri-patternmodeller -f corpus.txt.colibri.dat -c corpus.txt.colibri.cls -t 3 -l 6 -s -P   # -s skipgrams, -t occurrence threshold, -l max length, -P print (see colibri-core docs)
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real: colibri's flexgrams natively model gapped patterns that plain n-gram counting can't, giving motif candidates without an HMM or MEME run; for bioinformaticians wanting a cheap, memory-efficient first pass on repeats/binding sites; the weirdness is a true abstraction match, not a gimmick.
chains.fragile_seam: Tokenization choice (codon frame vs fixed-k vs amino acids) determines everything; wrong frame yields garbage, and colibri has no biological alphabet awareness so reverse-complement motifs are invisible unless you also feed the RC strand.

chains.roles: source: netsniff-ng captures and its fields are rendered as a token stream -> transform: each packet becomes a CG-3 'cohort' (surface form + candidate 'readings' = possible flow roles), and hand-written constraint-grammar rules disambiguate a packet's role using variable-distance context (SELECT/REMOVE readings if a SYN appears N cohorts back, etc.) -> sink: the disambiguated tagged stream feeds Siembol as enriched events for alerting
chains.glue: hop1: netsniff-ng / tshark field export -> awk formats CG cohort text (one packet = a "<pkt>" line, readings as tab-indented \"role\" TAGS). hop2: vislcg3 -g flows.cg3 reads cohort stdin, writes disambiguated cohort stdout. hop3: parse tags back to JSON -> Siembol Kafka/JSON ingestion
chains.emergent_capability: Stateful, context-sensitive flow classification over arbitrary packet distances written as declarative linguistic rules instead of a DPI signature engine or a stream-processor state machine.
chains.sketch: netsniff-ng --in eth0 --out - -s | tshark -r - -T fields -e frame.number -e ip.src -e tcp.flags | awk '{print "\"<p"$1">\""; print "\t\"handshake\" SYN"; print "\t\"data\" PSH"}' | vislcg3 -g flows.cg3   # rule e.g.:  SELECT (data) IF (-1* (handshake) BARRIER (reset)) ;  (see cg3 docs for exact rule syntax)
chains.pattern: rule-engine repurposing (disambiguator as classifier over non-text cohorts)
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real: CG-3's BARRIER / variable-distance context operators express 'this packet is X only if no RST intervenes since a SYN' far more concisely than regex or awk, and no single pool tool does context-window disambiguation; for a threat hunter who wants human-auditable, order-sensitive flow labels; not friction-novelty because CG cohorts and packet-with-candidate-roles are the same data shape.
chains.fragile_seam: The cohort serialization throughput bottleneck — CG-3 is line-oriented text, so wire-speed capture must be batched/sampled, and readings must be pre-enumerated before rules can prune them.

chains.roles: source: a time-ordered stack of scientific rasters (Nanocubes heatmap exports, DEM time-series, microscopy, sensor fields) normalized to an image sequence -> transform: VapourSynth loads them as 'video frames' and runs mvtools motion estimation + temporal degrain, treating physical drift as camera motion -> sink: cleaned frames / y4m out to ffmpeg for an inspection movie or back to TIFF
chains.glue: hop1: magick normalizes each frame to same-size 16-bit PNG sequence frame%05d.png. hop2: VapourSynth script uses core.imwri.Read(sequence) -> core.mv.Analyse/core.mv.Degrain2 -> y4m via vspipe. hop3: vspipe script.vpy - --y4m | ffmpeg -i - out.mp4 (or imwri.Write back to tiff)
chains.emergent_capability: Motion-compensated video denoising (which averages along estimated motion, not naively across time) cleans scientific time-series while preserving moving fronts that a plain temporal mean would smear.
chains.sketch:
magick mogrify -path seq -depth 16 -resize 512x512! frames/*.tif; cat > dn.vpy <<'PY'
import vapoursynth as vs
c=vs.core
clip=c.imwri.Read(['seq/%05d.png'%i for i in range(200)])
sup=c.mv.Super(clip); bv=c.mv.Analyse(sup,isb=True); fv=c.mv.Analyse(sup,isb=False)
clip=c.mv.Degrain1(clip,sup,bv,fv,thsad=400)
clip.set_output()
PY
vspipe dn.vpy - --y4m | ffmpeg -i - denoised.mp4
chains.pattern: cross-domain filter-graph reuse (video temporal ops on non-video stacks)
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real: mvtools follows optical-flow motion so a propagating wavefront/plume stays sharp where a boxcar temporal average destroys it, and no imaging/vis tool in the pool does motion-compensated temporal filtering; for a scientist with noisy time-lapse fields; not friction because the 'frames are a movie' framing is legitimate and buys real motion estimation.
chains.fragile_seam: mvtools assumes photometric constancy and small inter-frame motion; if the physical field changes intensity (not just moves) or jumps between frames, motion vectors are wrong and it hallucinates smearing.

chains.roles: source: a Brainfuck program that prints a secret, assembled into a MIDI file whose note events encode the BF opcodes -> transform: the single MIDI file is polysemous — Schoenberg interprets it as a program that emits the secret, while Nallely plays it as (atonal) generative music -> sink: recipient runs schoenberg on the shared 'music' MIDI to recover the message; optionally PaulStretch smears the rendered audio into an ambient drone as the public cover performance
chains.glue: hop1: BF ops -> MIDI note-on sequence (Schoenberg's Brainfuck-to-MIDI mapping). hop2a: schoenberg run secret.mid -> stdout text; hop2b: MIDI over Nallely's MIDI/websocket in to a synth voice. hop3: render WAV -> PaulStretch WAV in/out for the ambient cover
chains.emergent_capability: One MIDI file is simultaneously a shareable piece of music and an executable that prints a hidden message — executable steganography inside a score.
chains.sketch:
schoenberg run secret.mid            # prints the hidden string (CLI per repo; exact subcommand see docs)
# perform it:  aplaymidi -p Nallely secret.mid   then  paulstretch performance.wav drone.wav -s 20 (see paulstretch args)
chains.pattern: polysemy / dual-interpretation artifact (same bytes read two ways)
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real: neither a stego tool nor a synth produces a file that is both valid music and a self-printing program — the covert channel lives in the interpretation, not in appended bytes, so it defeats byte-level stegdetectors; for CTF authors and hacktivist artists ('the recital contained the manifesto'); the risk is tooling, not concept.
chains.fragile_seam: There may be no ready BF->MIDI assembler in the Schoenberg repo, so the note sequence encoding the program likely has to be hand-crafted or scripted, and any MIDI-editing/transposition by an intermediary corrupts the opcodes.

chains.glue: Pastvu HTTP API returns JSON photo records with {geo:[lat,lon], year} -> jq flattens to CSV rows (lat,lon,year,type) -> hand-written Nanocubes .map config declares a spatial dim (lat/lon quadtree), a temporal dim (year), and categorical dims -> `nanocube create` builds the binary .nanocube index -> `nanocube serve` exposes the OLAP query API over HTTP -> browser heatmap.
chains.emergent_capability: Turns a crowdsourced historical-photo archive into a billion-scale interactive spatiotemporal density surface you can time-brush and drill, which Pastvu's own point-plot Leaflet map cannot do.
chains.sketch: curl 'https://pastvu.com/api2?method=photo.getByBounds¶ms={...bbox...}' | jq -r '.result.photos[] | [.geo[0],.geo[1],.year,.type] | @csv' > past.csv; nanocube create past.csv past.map past.nanocube; nanocube serve past.nanocube --port 51234  (exact .map field syntax: see nanocube docs)
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real: multiscale density + temporal histograms are a different analytic object than a pin map. So-what survives: urban historians and preservationists get 'when was this block most photographed' at interactive speed. Not friction-weird.
chains.roles: source: Pastvu API feed -> transform: jq to CSV + .map schema -> sink: Nanocubes HTTP heatmap
chains.fragile_seam: Pastvu API pagination/rate limits and the year field being coarse or missing on many photos; sparse temporal data weakens the cube's histogram dimension.

chains.glue: A large corpus of ordinary human-composed .mid files (never intended as code) is streamed one file at a time into Schoenberg, whose semantics interpret note events as a Brainfuck tape/pointer/loop program: each .mid -> `schoenberg run` -> stdout bytes + halt/nonhalt behavior -> a driver filters for files that halt AND emit non-empty, non-trivial output -> the surviving 'found programs' are rendered as a slideshow.
chains.emergent_capability: Mines a music corpus for MIDI files that are accidentally valid, halting, output-producing Brainfuck programs — 'found computation' latent in human melody.
chains.sketch: find lakh/ -name '*.mid' | xargs -I{} sh -c 'timeout 2 schoenberg run "{}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q . && echo FOUND {}' ; curate hits into found.md and present with `patat found.md`  (schoenberg run/exec subcommand: see repo docs)
chains.verdict_reason: Genuine idea-collision (an esolang's parser weaponizes a music dataset as a program search space), and no single tool does it. But the payoff is aesthetic/curiosity for esolang and generative-art people, not utilitarian — honestly a wildcard, not a workhorse.
chains.roles: source: MIDI dataset -> transform: Schoenberg BF interpreter + halt/output filter -> sink: patat curated deck
chains.fragile_seam: Almost all MIDI either fails to parse as a well-formed program or trivially halts with empty output; the yield of interesting hits may be near-zero without loosening 'non-trivial'.

chains.glue: stegify embeds a payload into a cover image via LSB -> the stego image is scored by Aletheia's pre-trained steganalysis model (`aletheia.py auto`), whose numeric detection probability is parsed from stdout -> a driver loop treats that probability as a fitness/loss signal, perturbing cover choice and embedding density to minimize it -> the best evaders are cross-checked against StegExpose's independent statistical-fusion detector to test whether evasion generalizes beyond the one model.
chains.emergent_capability: Repurposes a steganalysis detector's own trained model as the fitness function of an evolutionary evasion attack — a detector becomes an evader-factory.
chains.sketch: for c in covers/*.png; do stegify encode --carrier $c --data secret.zip --result out.png; s=$(python3 aletheia.py auto out.png | awk '/prob/{print $NF}'); echo "$s $c"; done | sort -n | head; java -jar StegExpose.jar bestdir/  (exact stegify subcommand flags & aletheia model name: see docs)
chains.verdict_reason: A detector run backwards as an optimizer is real emergence no single tool ships. So-what survives: steganalysis researchers and red teams get a concrete robustness benchmark and adversarial-example generator. The two-judge cross-check kills the 'you only fooled one model' objection.
chains.roles: source: stegify stego images -> transform: Aletheia model score -> loop back to stegify params -> sink: StegExpose generalization test
chains.fragile_seam: Aletheia's score is only differentiable-by-search here (black-box), so convergence is slow; and gains against the ML model may not transfer to StegExpose's statistical detectors, exposing overfitting to one judge.

tools: SRAM Dumper firmware (Namco System2x6, dump artifacts)
chains.glue: The dumper firmware emits many sramX.bin snapshots taken across different arcade settings/states (the binary dumps are the fuel) -> each dump is tokenized into a text stream of fixed-width byte 'words' (od -> whitespace-separated hex tokens, one line per record window) -> `colibri-classencode` + `colibri-patternmodeller -s` build a compressed pattern model over that byte-token corpus, mining recurring n-grams AND skipgrams -> stable n-grams reveal headers/magic, skipgrams ('fixed ... variable ... fixed') reveal record framing and checksum positions -> pattern graph rendered with dot.
chains.emergent_capability: Unsupervised reverse-engineering of an undocumented arcade SRAM layout by treating firmware dumps as a language and letting an NLP skipgram miner surface the record grammar.
chains.sketch: for f in sram*.bin; do od -An -tx1 -w16 $f | awk '{print}'; done > corpus.txt; colibri-classencode corpus.txt; colibri-patternmodeller -f corpus.colibri.dat -c corpus.colibri.cls -t 2 -l 8 -s -P  (skipgram threshold/length flags: see colibri-core docs)
chains.verdict_reason: Skipgrams are literally the right shape for 'fixed field / variable body / checksum', and nobody reaches for a Finnish-morphology-era NLP tool to crack arcade SRAM. So-what survives: hardware preservationists get candidate field boundaries without a datasheet. Emergence is real (colibri finds structure od alone never surfaces).
chains.roles: source: firmware .bin dumps -> transform: byte tokenization -> colibri skipgram model -> sink: graphviz format map
chains.fragile_seam: Tokenization window/alignment choice dominates results — pick the wrong byte stride and real records straddle token boundaries, so every discovered 'pattern' is an artifact of the window, not the format.

chains.glue: Justlog's REST API serves full channel/user chat histories as JSON -> jq extracts message text and collapses it to a frequency word-list (word<TAB>count) -> `morfessor-train` runs MAP-estimation unsupervised segmentation over that word-list, learning morpheme boundaries with no dictionary -> `morfessor-segment` splits novel emote-compounds and spam-mutations into morphemes -> fzf lets you interactively browse the learned segmentation of internet-native neologisms.
chains.emergent_capability: Discovers the productive morphology of a live online micro-dialect (emote compounding, suffix spam, meme derivations) straight from raw chat, with zero lexicon.
chains.sketch: curl 'https://logs.justlog.xyz/channel/CH/user/U?json' | jq -r '.messages[].text' | tr ' ' '\n' | sort | uniq -c | awk '{print $2" "$1}' > words.txt; morfessor-train words.txt -s emote.model; morfessor-segment -l emote.model words.txt | fzf  (endpoint & flags: see justlog/morfessor docs)
chains.verdict_reason: A morphological-segmentation model built for Finnish/Turkish aimed at PogChampionship-style emote agglutination is a real collision, and Morfessor surfaces structure a word-count never would. So-what survives: sociolinguists and platform-culture researchers get quantitative morpheme inventories of a dialect with no dictionary.
chains.roles: source: Justlog chat feed -> transform: jq word-list -> Morfessor model -> sink: fzf segmentation browser
chains.fragile_seam: Chat is noisy (URLs, unicode spam, code-switching); without aggressive frequency thresholding Morfessor learns junk morphemes, and per-channel emote sets may not generalize across communities.

chains.chain_name: Genomic Grammar: DNA disambiguated by a linguist's rules
chains.roles: source: smof streams codons out of a FASTA genome -> transform A: colibri-core mines flexgrams (variable-gap motifs) to derive candidate 'grammar' rules -> transform B: awk reshapes codons into CG-3 cohort text -> sink: vislcg3 applies context-dependent rules to disambiguate/annotate ambiguous reading frames and motif boundaries
chains.glue: smof stdout (FASTA/plain text) -> awk emits CG-3 cohort format ('"<AGT>"' header line, then TAB-indented readings '\t"AGT" CODON START?'); vislcg3 -g grammar.cg3 reads that cohort stream on stdin and writes an annotated cohort stream on stdout. colibri-core is fed the same corpus via colibri-classencode -> colibri-patternmodeller (-s skipgrams) and its high-frequency flexgrams are hand-lifted into CG-3 REMOVE/SELECT rules.
chains.emergent_capability: Reading-frame and motif-boundary disambiguation on DNA using the exact context-over-distance machinery built for resolving grammatical ambiguity in human language.
chains.sketch:
smof translate -f genome.fna \
 | awk '{for(i=1;i<=length($0)-2;i+=3){c=substr($0,i,3); print "\"<"c">\""; print "\t\""c"\" CODON"}}' > codons.cg
# derive candidate rules from variable-gap motifs
colibri-classencode corpus.txt && colibri-patternmodeller -f corpus.colibri.dat -t 2 -l 9 -s -P
# apply the hand-written constraint grammar (SELECT/REMOVE over distance)
vislcg3 -g motif.cg3 < codons.cg > annotated.cg   # see cg3 docs for rule syntax
chains.pattern: misapplied-engine (pattern-over-distance solver transplanted to a non-language token stream)
chains.fragile_seam: CG-3 rules assume linguistic locality; biological long-range dependencies (enhancers, secondary structure) blow past the window the grammar can express, and codon-to-cohort framing bakes in a frame assumption the grammar is supposed to be discovering.
chains.verdict_reason: Real emergence: neither smof nor cg3 alone annotates motifs by learned context; the colliding idea (grammar disambiguation == frame disambiguation) is genuine, and the audience is clear — computational biologists who want interpretable, rule-based motif calls instead of a black-box HMM.

chains.chain_name: Cartography of the Wire: browsing a billion packets as IP-space geography
chains.roles: source: netsniff-ng zero-copy captures/replays packets to pcap and prints per-packet fields -> transform: awk maps 32-bit src/dst IPs onto a Hilbert-curve (x,y) 'continent' and emits time,x,y,bytes CSV + a .map -> sink: Nanocubes indexes the CSV into an in-memory cube served over HTTP, browsed as a zoomable heatmap where geography IS the IPv4 address space
chains.glue: netsniff-ng --in cap.pcap --out - (printed packet records) -> awk (Hilbert encode IP octets -> x,y) -> CSV rows time,lat=x,lon=y,bytes; nanocube create consumes CSV + .map schema and nanocube serve exposes the HTTP query/tile API that caddy fronts to the browser viewer.
chains.emergent_capability: Interactive spatiotemporal OLAP over raw traffic where scan sweeps, DDoS fan-in and botnet C2 appear as literal geographic clusters and migrations in IP-space-time.
chains.sketch:
netsniff-ng --in cap.pcap --out - -s \
 | awk '/IP/{ip=$srcfield; split(ip,o,"."); \
 # hilbert_d2xy(o[1..4]) -> x,y  (see xkcd 195 / Hilbert IP map)
 print ts","x","y","len}' > wire.csv
nanocube create wire.csv wire.map wire.nanocube   # per pool CLI; see nanocube docs
nanocube serve wire.nanocube & caddy reverse-proxy --to :29512
chains.pattern: coordinate-remap (project a non-geographic key space into lat/lon so a geo-analytics engine becomes a general OLAP surface)
chains.fragile_seam: Parsing netsniff-ng's printed record format and computing a correct Hilbert d2xy in awk is brittle; getting the .map cardinality/quadtree depth right for a 32-bit synthetic coordinate space is the make-or-break step.
chains.verdict_reason: A single tool can't do it — Nanocubes needs geo coordinates, netsniff-ng has none, and the Hilbert remap is the emergent bridge that makes billions of packets navigable; it serves SOC/threat-hunt analysts who already think in the xkcd IP-map mental model.

chains.chain_name: Dead-Drop Hunter: steganalysis over a public geotagged photo archive
chains.roles: source: Creepy/Pastvu aggregate geotagged public photos to CSV/KML with coordinates -> transform A: curl bulk-fetches the images -> transform B: StegExpose fuses RS/Sample-Pairs/Chi-Square for a fast bulk suspicion score, Aletheia's ML models confirm the survivors -> sink: SedonaDB joins suspicion scores back to coordinates and Nanocubes renders where/when covert-carrier images cluster
chains.glue: Creepy file export (CSV/KML) -> curl -O per URL -> local image dir -> java -jar StegExpose.jar dir default report.csv (stdout/CSV) -> Aletheia auto on flagged files -> SedonaDB reads the CSV as a table, spatial-joins to photo coords (WKT), exports GeoParquet/CSV -> nanocube create for the time-animated heatmap.
chains.emergent_capability: Turns an open crowdsourced photo map into a counter-intelligence sensor that surfaces likely steganographic dead-drops by their geographic and temporal clustering.
chains.sketch:
# 1 harvest coords
creepy  # export targets.csv (lat,lon,url,time)
# 2 pull images
awk -F, 'NR>1{print $3}' targets.csv | xargs -P8 -I{} curl -sO {}
# 3 bulk + confirm
java -jar StegExpose.jar ./imgs default stego.csv
aletheia.py auto ./imgs   # ML confirmation, see aletheia docs
# 4 map suspects
duckdb/sedona: SELECT * FROM 'stego.csv' s JOIN targets t USING(fname) WHERE s.above_thr;
nanocube create suspects.csv suspects.map suspects.nanocube
chains.pattern: cross-corpus-detector (harvest one domain's public exhaust, run another domain's forensic classifier, re-project the hits)
chains.fragile_seam: StegExpose/Aletheia false-positive rates are high on heavily recompressed social-media JPEGs, so the geographic 'cluster' can be an artifact of one camera/app pipeline rather than a real dead-drop — the join is only as honest as the steganalysis threshold.
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real (no tool in the pool both harvests geo-photos and steganalyzes them at scale), the 'so what' survives — CI researchers and abuse teams genuinely hunt image-based dead-drops — and the weirdness is idea-collision, not friction.

chains.chain_name: Atonal Computation Drone: hear a Brainfuck program run, stretched to a cathedral
chains.roles: source: a MIDI file that is simultaneously a Schoenberg (Brainfuck-semantics) program -> transform A: Schoenberg executes it for the computational output -> transform B: fluidsynth renders the same MIDI to audio -> transform C: PaulStretch time-stretches it 20x into an ambient drone -> optional sink: FreqTweak sculpts the spectrum live over JACK
chains.glue: program.mid is one file feeding two consumers: node schoenberg run program.mid (tape/pointer/loop execution -> stdout) AND fluidsynth -F out.wav sf2 program.mid (MIDI -> WAV); PaulStretch reads WAV, writes stretched WAV; FreqTweak takes it over JACK audio I/O.
chains.emergent_capability: A single artifact that is at once source code, a running computation, and a piece of drone music — you literally listen to the atonal texture of an algorithm executing.
chains.sketch:
node schoenberg run add.mid          # executes as Brainfuck; prints result (see schoenberg docs)
fluidsynth -F add.wav /usr/share/sf2/FluidR3.sf2 add.mid
paulstretch add.wav drone.wav -s 20.0 -w 0.5   # extreme stretch; see paulstretch_cpp docs
# optional live spectral sculpt over JACK:
freqtweak   # connect drone.wav playback -> freqtweak in
chains.pattern: dual-representation (one file inhabits two incompatible semantics — executable and musical — at once)
chains.fragile_seam: MIDI-to-audio synthesis is the whole hinge: without a soundfont + fluidsynth (ffmpeg alone won't synth MIDI), there's no waveform to stretch; and a program optimized to compute is not optimized to sound good, so 'delightful' is not guaranteed.
chains.verdict_reason: Barely practical but genuinely beautiful: the emergence (code == music == computation in one object) cannot be faked by any single tool, and it's for sound artists / esolang lovers who want to perform an algorithm. Weirdness is pure idea-collision.

chains.chain_name: Rivers of the Face: watershed hydrology run on a photograph
chains.roles: source: any photo -> transform A: magick converts brightness to a floating-point grayscale 'elevation' GeoTIFF (fake DEM) -> transform B: TauDEM runs pit-removal, D-Infinity flow direction, and flow accumulation as if the image were terrain -> sink: magick/pixelsort renders the extracted stream network back as generative glitch art of rivers that never existed
chains.glue: magick portrait.jpg -colorspace Gray -depth 32 -define quantum:format=floating-point dem.tif (GeoTIFF the DEM) -> TauDEM MPI executables consume/emit GeoTIFF rasters (pitremove -> dinfflowdir -> areadinf) -> magick -auto-level on the flow-accumulation raster -> pixelsort along the drainage lines for the final image.
chains.emergent_capability: D-Infinity watershed delineation becomes a generative-art engine: the 'rivers', ridgelines and basins of a human face emerge from real hydrological math applied to luminance-as-topography.
chains.sketch:
magick portrait.jpg -colorspace Gray -depth 32 -define quantum:format=floating-point dem.tif
# TauDEM needs a georeferenced GeoTIFF; stamp a synthetic transform (see TauDEM docs)
pitremove -z geo.tif -fel fel.tif
dinfflowdir -fel fel.tif -ang ang.tif -slp slp.tif
areadinf -ang ang.tif -sca sca.tif           # flow accumulation = river brightness
magick sca.tif -auto-level rivers.png && pixelsort rivers.png -o final.png
chains.pattern: domain-transplant (feed a physics/GIS solver an input from a domain where its governing equations are meaningless, harvest the aesthetics of the misapplication)
chains.fragile_seam: TauDEM expects a properly georeferenced GeoTIFF with a valid geotransform; a magick-written TIFF usually lacks one, so without a gdal_translate -a_srs/-a_ullr step the MPI tools refuse or produce degenerate flow — the georef stamp is the crux.
chains.verdict_reason: Absurd-but-beautiful and irreducible to one tool: TauDEM has no notion of art, magick has no notion of watersheds, and the collision (luminance == elevation) produces imagery neither could. For generative artists and cartography nerds who want hydrologically 'true' fictional maps.

chains.roles: SOURCE: jvarkit/bioalcidae streams per-variant records out of a VCF via a JS/Java expression -> TRANSFORM: duckdb projects genomic (contig,start,AF) into a synthetic (lat,lon,time,category) tuple space and emits CSV + .map -> SINK: Nanocubes builds an in-memory hierarchical cube and serves it as a browser heatmap/histogram over HTTP.
chains.glue: hop1: jvarkit stdout = CSV lines (one per variant); hop2: duckdb reads CSV, writes Nanocubes-shaped CSV + a .map field-mapping file (file); hop3: nanocube reads CSV+.map, serves an HTTP query API + web viewer.
chains.emergent_capability: Pan/zoom a billion genomic variants at 60fps with live brushed histograms, using a geo-heatmap engine that has never heard of DNA.
chains.sketch:
java -jar bioalcidaejdk.jar -e 'stream().forEach(V->println(V.getContig()+","+V.getStart()+","+V.getAttributeAsString("AF","0")))' in.vcf > v.csv
duckdb -c "COPY (SELECT (start % 1000000)/10000.0 - 50 AS lat, (start / 1000000) % 360 - 180 AS lon, contig AS cat, make_timestamp(2000,1,1,0,0, CAST(af AS DOUBLE)*1e6) AS t FROM read_csv_auto('v.csv',names=['contig','start','af'])) TO 'nc.csv' (HEADER)"
nanocube create nc.csv nc.map out.nanocube && nanocube serve out.nanocube   # exact create/serve flags + .map schema: see docs (github.com/laurolins/nanocube)
chains.verdict_reason: Emergence is real (no single genomics browser gives billion-scale interactive cube brushing for free); the 'so what' survives — population geneticists get IGV-at-scale exploration; weirdness is from the geo-cube/DNA collision, not friction.
chains.fragile_seam: The coordinate embedding: you must map genomic coordinates into valid, non-colliding lat/lon/time bins, and the exact `nanocube create` CLI + .map column-type schema is under-documented and version-sensitive.

chains.roles: SOURCE: netsniff-ng dissects live packets to stdout -> TRANSFORM: awk rewrites each packet as a CG-3 'cohort' (a surface token + a bag of tags like proto/flags/port) -> ENGINE/SINK: vislcg3 runs a constraint grammar as a long-lived stream filter, applying context-dependent rules that reason ACROSS packets (variable distance) to add/remove classification tags, emitting a disambiguated alert stream.
chains.glue: hop1: netsniff-ng human-readable per-packet dissection on stdout; hop2: awk emits CG cohort text ("<10.0.0.1>\n\t\"tcp\" SYN sport:443\n"); hop3: vislcg3 -g reads the cohort stream from the pipe and writes tagged cohorts to stdout — cg3 is the daemonized long-running process.
chains.emergent_capability: Write TCP-flow intrusion logic as linguist-style context rules ('REMOVE Benign IF (-1 SYN)(0 SYNACK)(1 ACK) far to the left'), getting cross-packet stateful reasoning with zero imperative code.
chains.sketch:
netsniff-ng -i eth0 --notouch-irq 2>/dev/null \
 | awk -f pkt2cohort.awk \
 | vislcg3 -g flow.cg3 > /var/log/flow-alerts    # flow.cg3: REMOVE (@benign) IF (-2 (\"tcp\" SYN)) (-1 (\"tcp\" SYNACK)) (0 (\"tcp\" ACK)) ; cg3 flag -g/--grammar is verified, cohort format per cg3 docs
chains.verdict_reason: A constraint-grammar disambiguator doing stateful packet-flow classification is a genuine idea collision, not plumbing; audience is DFIR/SOC engineers who want declarative multi-packet rules. Neither tool alone reasons over both grammar-distance and packet order.
chains.fragile_seam: netsniff-ng's dissection output is human-readable, not a stable machine format, so the awk cohort-izer is brittle; cg3's left/right context rules assume in-order tokens, so any reordering or drop corrupts the 'sentence'.

chains.roles: TRANSFORM/RED: stegify LSB-embeds a payload into a carrier image -> WATCHER: watchexec fires on every new carrier/payload combo -> BLUE/SINK: Aletheia's ML steganalysis scores the stego image, and the score is appended to a growing labeled dataset that drives the next payload-size choice.
chains.glue: hop1: stegify encode writes stego.png (file); hop2: watchexec -w watches the carriers/ dir and re-runs the pair on change (process spawn); hop3: Aletheia reads stego.png + pretrained model, prints detection probability to stdout appended to scores.tsv (file).
chains.emergent_capability: A self-playing red/blue loop that auto-discovers the exact payload capacity threshold where LSB hiding becomes ML-detectable — and drops a labeled ROC dataset as a byproduct.
chains.sketch:
watchexec -w carriers/ -w payloads/ -- '\
 for c in carriers/*.png; do\
   stegify encode --carrier "$c" --data payloads/next.bin --result out/$(basename $c) &&\
   python3 aletheia.py auto out/$(basename $c) | tee -a scores.tsv;\
 done'   # stegify encode/decode subcommands verified; aletheia.py auto/detector cmd: see docs (daniellerch/aletheia)
chains.verdict_reason: Neither tool self-plays; wiring them through a watcher creates an adversarial threshold-finder and free training data. For steganalysis researchers and CTF authors this is directly useful, not novelty-from-friction.
chains.fragile_seam: Aletheia's pretrained models are method-specific; if 'auto' picks the wrong detector for stegify's exact LSB scheme the scores are meaningless, and nothing guarantees the payload-tuning loop converges rather than oscillates.

chains.roles: SOURCE-A: QuackOSM extracts buildings/waterways from an OSM PBF to GeoParquet -> SOURCE-B: TauDEM runs D-infinity pit-fill/flow/watershed on a DEM raster to delineate basins -> JOIN/SINK: duckdb spatial does ST_Within to assign every OSM building to its hydrological basin and rank flood exposure.
chains.glue: hop1: quackosm writes .parquet (GeoParquet, EPSG:4326); hop2: TauDEM CLI chain reads GeoTIFF DEM, writes basins raster + stream shapefile (file); hop3: duckdb LOAD spatial reads both and joins with ST_Within (SQL over Arrow-backed geometry).
chains.emergent_capability: Turn a raw OSM extract + a raw DEM into per-building flood-basin exposure with one SQL join — no desktop GIS, no manual digitizing.
chains.sketch:
quackosm region.osm.pbf --geom-filter-file bbox.geojson > osm.parquet   # buildings/waterways
mpiexec -n 8 pitremove -z dem.tif -fel fel.tif
mpiexec -n 8 dinfflowdir -fel fel.tif -ang ang.tif -slp slp.tif
mpiexec -n 8 areadinf -ang ang.tif -sca sca.tif
streamnet -fel fel.tif -p p.tif -ad8 ad8.tif -src src.tif -ord ord.tif -tree tree.txt -coord coord.txt -net stream.shp -w basins.tif
duckdb -c "INSTALL spatial;LOAD spatial; SELECT b.osm_id, r.basin FROM 'osm.parquet' b, ST_Read('basins.tif') r WHERE ST_Within(b.geometry, r.geom)"
chains.verdict_reason: The fusion (OSM assets scored against MPI-parallel D-infinity basins, joined in-process) is not something one tool does; audience is flood insurers and municipal planners without ArcGIS budgets. Payoff is concrete and the seam is real work.
chains.fragile_seam: CRS and resolution alignment — OSM is lon/lat EPSG:4326 while the DEM/basins raster is usually projected; ST_Within silently returns nothing if projections aren't reconciled first.

chains.roles: SOURCE/SYNC: Entangled tangles a Markdown literate document into an odexp model file (and stitches results back) -> WATCHER: watchexec re-fires on every save of the .md -> SOLVER/SINK: odexp re-solves the ODE/SDE/DDE, runs linear stability analysis, and emits a gnuplot figure that Entangled stitches back into the prose.
chains.glue: hop1: Entangled tangle writes model.ode from fenced code blocks (file, noweb); hop2: watchexec -w model.md -e md spawns the pipeline on save (fs event); hop3: odexp -f model.ode reads the model + a batch command file, writes gnuplot PNG/data (file), then entangled stitch pulls outputs back into the Markdown.
chains.emergent_capability: A prose document where editing the sentence next to a differential equation instantly re-solves it and re-renders its phase portrait and stability class inline — a live bifurcation notebook built from a tangle daemon and a REPL solver.
chains.sketch:
watchexec -w model.md -e md -- '\
 entangled tangle && \
 odexp -f lorenz.ode < replot.cmds && \
 entangled stitch'   # Entangled tangle/stitch + watch daemon: see docs (entangled.github.io); odexp batch/stability + gnuplot output: see docs (github.com/samubernard/odexp)
chains.verdict_reason: Real emergence — Entangled only syncs text and odexp only solves; together, gated by a watcher, they become a live computational essay with stability analysis, which neither offers. Slightly niche audience (dynamical-systems educators/researchers) keeps it a wildcard rather than a slam-dunk.
chains.fragile_seam: odexp is interactive-first; driving it non-interactively to produce a deterministic figure per save (the batch command file + gnuplot handoff) is the weak joint, and Entangled's stitch must re-absorb a binary/image output it was designed for text around.
